user.title: Connect to Brickset
user.description: This integration reads your LEGO collection from Brickset.com. Get a free API key from your Brickset account under {api_key_path}, then sign in below. Your password is used once to obtain a token and is never stored.

data_description.api_key: Issued from your Brickset account under Tools, Web services.
data_description.username: The account whose owned and wanted sets should be tracked.
data_description.password: Exchanged for a long-lived token; only the token is saved.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect to Brickset
reauth_confirm.description: Brickset rejected the saved token for {username}. Confirm your API key and password to reconnect.

reconfigure.title: Change Brickset account
reconfigure.description: Update the API key or switch to a different Brickset account.

region.title: Pricing region
region.description: Prices and availability dates come from one LEGO.com market. Home Assistant reports your country as {country}; change the market if you buy from a different store.

data_description.region: Which LEGO.com market supplies recommended retail prices and retirement dates.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Brickset. Check your internet connection and try again.
error.invalid_auth: Brickset rejected that username or password.

abort.already_configured: That Brickset account is already set up.
abort.account_mismatch: That is a different Brickset account. Use a new entry instead of reconfiguring this one.

init.title: LEGO options
init.description: Brickset allows 100 catalogue calls per API key per day. Your current settings use about {estimated_calls} of your {budget} call budget.

data.themes: Themes to watch for new releases
data.catalogue_rich: Include set names in the index
data.panel: Show the LEGO panel in the sidebar

data_description.region: Which LEGO.com market supplies recommended retail prices and retirement dates.
data_description.themes: Each watched theme costs one API call per refresh.
data_description.watchlist: Full set numbers including the variant, for example 10497-1.
data_description.collection_interval_hours: How often owned and wanted sets are refreshed.
data_description.feeds_interval_hours: How often watched themes are checked for new sets.
data_description.daily_call_budget: Polling stops once this many calls have been made, leaving headroom for manual actions.
data_description.catalogue: Downloads the public LEGO set list so searching and checking a set number costs no Brickset calls. Uses no part of your daily allowance.
data_description.catalogue_rich: Names make the index searchable, at roughly 1.8 MB instead of 450 KB. Turn off on a storage-constrained machine, and search falls back to set numbers only.
data_description.catalogue_interval: How often the public LEGO set list is re-downloaded. The source is rebuilt nightly and gains roughly five sets a day; a set the index has not heard of still works, it just costs one Brickset call to look up.
data_description.panel: Adds a page for browsing your collection, your wishlist and new releases in the themes you follow. Turning it off removes the sidebar entry.

no_changes.message: Provide at least one field to change.

search_needs_criteria.message: Provide a query, theme or year to search for.

catalogue_disabled.message: The local set index is turned off for this account. Turn it on in the integration options first.

catalogue_unavailable.message: Could not download the set list. Check Home Assistant's internet access and try again.
